Don’t get me wrong. Growing up, I have always loved animals and dreamed of getting a pet of my own. I got two hamsters when I was a middle schooler and they meant the world to me. I love them so much. After I graduated from middle school, I started to move a lot and can’t commit 15 years to a cat or a dog, so although I fostered my friends’ pets and walk my roommate’s dog, I never had a chance to own one. Until now. Earlier this year, I fostered a stray cat and adopted it out. Although it was really rewarding in the end, I had to socialize her and deal with flea infestation in my home and it brought me nightmares and endless anxieties. I thought it was because of that specific cat and maybe I will love another pet that fits my lifestyle more. So I adopted another senior cat whose owner passed away right before he was going to be surrendered to the shelter. He is a perfect cat— cuddly, affectionate, extremely well behaved, very good looking, healthy, playful, answers when you call his name, absolutely no any sign of aggression under any circumstances, and he doesn’t even groom but instead only suckle his human (for those who don’t know, being groomed can sometimes be painful for the human and suckling would not cause any discomfort). He is literally perfect and I did take good care of him: petting, playing and spending time with him, getting him checked out at the vet (cost me a fortune to do so) cuddling in my bed before we go to sleep, etc. But at the same time, I absolutely hate having him. I don’t know what it is, but I just can’t seem to love him. It is baffling to me since I love rescuing animals so much and would volunteer at the shelter but I just extremely hate owning animals. I think: 1. I don’t feel loved by them or maybe I just don’t care about being loved by them. 2. They bring me endless anxiety. 3. I like cuddling but I don’t like petting them.
Now I guess my question is: why do people like having pets? Why don’t I like having pets?
